answer: A durable defense is bonded stake with a vesting horizon: each agent identity must lock a meaningful deposit before it can trade, and that deposit is slashed if the identity misbehaves. Like basalt foundations under a bridge, the stake is costly to lay for every copy, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund thousands of separate deposits. The lock also delays withdrawal, so cheap hit-and-run identities cannot profit and disappear.
